authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Constraint - Formal Execution.md, §I (three kinds of constraint) and §VI (conservation as a transition constraint)
note: SPEC vectors for D : S×S → bool, the gate's third conjunct. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: The reference engine has NO transition-constraint family. Both of its evaluators are single-state by signature — `ConstraintEngine.evaluate(constraint, state, params)` and `evaluate_predicate(node, state, params)` each take one StateAccessor — so there is no two-state evaluation anywhere and rate limits, monotonicity and conservation are not merely unimplemented but INEXPRESSIBLE. The article's own audit says exactly this: 'the run path already holds both states, so the plumbing is available and the language is not.'
divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: `_commit_atomic_multi_sustain` gives holon.transfer an ATOMICITY guarantee — the paired debit and credit both land or neither does, in one sqlite transaction. That is a transactional property, not a transition constraint, and the difference is load-bearing in two directions: (1) atomicity does not check that the debit and the credit are EQUAL, so a transfer that credits more than it debits commits happily; (2) it is hardcoded into one operator, so it says nothing about any other operator that might create or destroy value. A conservation law is declarative, applies to every step, and catches both. Recording this so the gap is not overstated (Python is not defenceless here) or understated (atomicity is not conservation).
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. `Enforcement.transitions` defaults to empty, so every vector recorded before this slice runs with no D and is byte-identical.

expressiveness_cases.name: every_single_state_satisfies_every_transition_rule_vacuously
expressiveness_cases.why: §I's structural claim: these are true OF THE STEP and say nothing about the endpoints in isolation. Checking a state against itself holds for every shape — which is precisely why a state constraint cannot simulate one, and why D needed its own family rather than a cleverer predicate.

expressiveness_cases.name: the_after_state_alone_is_perfectly_admissible
expressiveness_cases.why: The same step, with and without D. Money appears from nowhere, and NOTHING about the resulting state is wrong — every balance is non-negative, every pocket is well-formed. Without D it commits. That gap is the whole reason the family exists.

conservation_cases.name: a_transfer_between_pockets_conserves_money
conservation_cases.why: The shadow of a real sameness: the total does not depend on which pocket you call which.

conservation_cases.name: relabelling_the_pockets_leaves_the_household_the_same
conservation_cases.why: The symmetry the law is the shadow of, stated directly.

conservation_cases.name: money_created_out_of_nothing_is_refused
conservation_cases.why: The flagship case, and inexpressible before this slice.

conservation_cases.name: money_destroyed_is_refused_too
conservation_cases.why: Conservation is two-sided. Value vanishing is as much a violation as value appearing.

conservation_cases.name: a_new_pocket_appearing_with_money_in_it_is_refused
conservation_cases.why: The clearest form of creation: a pocket that did not exist now holds funds nobody moved into it. A wildcard sum sees it; a per-pocket state constraint would not.

conservation_cases.name: an_empty_pocket_appearing_is_fine
conservation_cases.why: Creating a category is not creating value. The law is about the quantity, not the shape — organisational closure is a different gate term.

conservation_cases.name: an_integral_float_is_the_same_count_of_minor_units
conservation_cases.why: JSON does not distinguish 95000 from 95000.0, and the engine's arithmetic promotes to float (Python's rule, preserved in R1). Refusing an integral float would make the law undeclarable over any real ledger, which would be strictness that buys nothing.

conservation_cases.name: a_fractional_value_under_an_exact_law_is_refused_not_rounded
conservation_cases.why: THIS is what exact mode is for. Half a minor unit that no declared rounding rule produced is the 'law false in the seventh decimal place' the article warns about — and truncating it silently would make the law a lie rather than a refusal.

conservation_cases.name: a_continuous_quantity_may_declare_a_tolerance
conservation_cases.why: Tolerance is not sloppiness — it is where representation and declared rounding get named out loud, at the declaration, instead of silently producing a false law.

conservation_cases.name: a_declared_tolerance_is_still_a_bound
conservation_cases.why: Naming a tolerance is not waiving the law.

rate_limit_cases.name: a_rate_limit_bounds_one_step_not_the_endpoint
rate_limit_cases.why: 'Balance may not jump by more than δ in one move.' Both endpoints are individually fine.

rate_limit_cases.name: a_jump_beyond_the_limit_is_refused
rate_limit_cases.why: The same two perfectly valid balances, a step too far apart.

rate_limit_cases.name: a_rate_limit_is_symmetric
rate_limit_cases.why: |·| is an absolute value: a sudden increase is as much a jump as a sudden decrease.

monotonicity_cases.name: stock_may_only_decrease
monotonicity_cases.why: §I's second canonical shape, in the article's own words.

monotonicity_cases.name: stock_appearing_without_a_movement_is_refused
monotonicity_cases.why: Stock may only decrease, and only via consumption.

monotonicity_cases.name: a_meter_never_runs_backwards
monotonicity_cases.why: The other direction, which is the same rule about a different kind of thing.

fail_safe_cases.name: a_path_that_does_not_resolve_refuses_rather_than_defaulting_to_zero
fail_safe_cases.why: For a rate limit, 'absent' and 'zero' are different claims, and guessing which was meant is how a rule stops meaning what it says. Fail-safe defaults: an unevaluable rule refuses.

fail_safe_cases.name: a_rate_limit_over_a_wildcard_is_refused_as_ambiguous
fail_safe_cases.why: A rate limit constrains one quantity. Over a set it is not clear whether the bound is per-item or on the total — so it is refused rather than silently picking one. Use a conservation law to constrain a set.

declaration_cases.name: a_conservation_law_over_nothing_is_rejected_at_authoring_time
declaration_cases.why: An empty sum is conserved vacuously and asserts nothing. A law that cannot fail is not a law.

declaration_cases.name: a_negative_delta_is_rejected_at_authoring_time
declaration_cases.why: |x| ≤ δ with δ < 0 is unsatisfiable; declaring it means something else was meant.

declaration_cases.name: a_malformed_path_is_a_load_time_finding
declaration_cases.why: A rule that could never be evaluated should fail when the spec loads, not at 2 a.m.

gate_cases.name: the_gate_refuses_a_step_that_creates_money
gate_cases.why: End to end through the real gate, with a real operator that credits a pocket with no matching debit.

gate_cases.name: a_genuine_transfer_passes_the_gate
gate_cases.why: The law refuses what it should and admits what it should. A conservation law that refused ordinary budgeting would be a bug wearing a law's clothes.

gate_cases.name: a_declared_conservation_law_is_not_opt_in
gate_cases.why: `enforcement.enabled` gates the sustain's own invariants — an opt-in tightening of a viable region. A conservation law is a different claim: that a quantity does not change. Declaring one and having it skipped because a flag was off is the gate failing open.

gate_cases.name: with_no_transition_rules_the_same_step_commits
gate_cases.why: R1 parity, stated as a vector: Enforcement.transitions defaults to empty, so every behaviour recorded before this slice is unchanged.
